title: Associate General Counsel, Energy & Regulatory
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for an Associate General Counsel, Energy & Regulatory to join our Legal team.

Position Description

The Associate General Counsel, Energy & Regulatory will play a critical role helping us navigate a wide range of energy-related legal, regulatory, and public policy matters, as we continue to develop, build, and scale our powerhouse fleet. We are looking for an attorney with 7-10 years of energy regulatory experience, with substantial experience managing FERC and State Public Utility Commission (PUC) engagements and submissions, and supporting interconnection applications.

This person’s primary responsibilities will be to lead our FERC, State PUC, and interconnection-related legal work, including representing Oklo in FERC and PUC proceedings and supporting interconnection agreements and processes. They will also support energy-related policy work, including monitoring and engaging in FERC and related regulatory rulemaking efforts, monitoring relevant policy developments with ISOs and RTOs, and working closely with our government affairs team on federal, state, and local legislative engagements. Beyond FERC and energy-related regulatory support, they will support other pre-construction regulatory and zoning efforts, including supporting environmental reviews and engagements, and local zoning and permitting work, leveraging outside counsel as needed. Note that we have a dedicated team to handle nuclear regulatory engagement with the NRC and Department of Energy, and that work is outside of the scope of this role (although you will certainly work in coordination with them on related matters).

This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge nuclear energy technology and energy regulatory law. The ideal candidate will have deep experience in FERC practice and energy project development, and will bring hands-on experience navigating complex regulatory approval processes. As a high-growth company, you will also help with other legal needs across the company as they arise. This role, which reports directly to our General Counsel, is perfect for an experienced energy regulatory attorney who is ready to roll up their sleeves and help a growing company navigate (and improve) a complex regulatory landscape.

We are not looking for someone who is looking to operate in a silo: we are a lean team and hire lawyers who are great at what they do, but are excited to do work beyond their areas of expertise. Oklo is growing fast and every day presents new opportunities and challenging legal questions—we care more about you and your ability to learn and grow than your specific substantive experience or which boxes you check. If you are someone who thrives in exciting and fast-moving environments, and are eager to grow and push yourself, this role may be for you.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Lead all FERC-related legal matters, including filings, compliance, and proceedings before FERC; advise on generator interconnection processes, wholesale power market rules, and transmission access matters;
  • Support energy-related public policy work, including monitoring FERC and other regulatory rulemakings and participating in comment processes;
  • Work closely with our government affairs team on federal, state, and local legislative and regulatory initiatives;
  • Support pre-construction regulatory and zoning work, including environmental reviews (NEPA and state equivalents), local permitting, land use approvals, and siting matters, managing outside counsel as needed;
  • Help to review and negotiate interconnection agreements, and support our commercial legal team with energy-related requirements in agreements being negotiated; and
  • Track regulatory developments across key jurisdictions and advise business teams on regulatory strategy and compliance risk.
  • Provide expertise and technical assistance supporting federal, state and local government affairs teams on legislation and policy analysis that could impact or improve outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • A J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school and admission to practice law in at least one U.S. state
  • 7–10 years of energy regulatory experience at a large law firm or in-house legal department
  • Substantive FERC practice experience, including experience with FERC filings, rulemakings, and proceedings
  • Experience with State PUC filings and matters
  • Experience with generator interconnection processes and/or transmission access matters, or other experience with state public utility commission proceedings
  • Experience with energy-related public policy and legislative affairs, and close collaboration with government affairs teams
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage and prioritize multiple matters simultaneously

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience working on data center related matters
  • Prior experience working at or with FERC or State PUCs
  • Experience working in-house at a high-growth or startup company
  • Familiarity with energy project permitting and pre-construction regulatory approvals, including NEPA and state environmental review
  • Experience supporting local zoning or permitting efforts
  • Interest in experimenting with AI and other tools
  • Nuclear and/or nuclear-adjacent technologies or renewables experience

Competencies

We are looking for a Associate General Counsel, Energy & Regulatory that is:

  • Deeply knowledgeable in FERC practice, power markets, and energy regulatory law, with hands-on experience in FERC proceedings and filings
  • Familiar with State Public Utility Commission processes
  • Experienced with generator interconnection processes, transmission access, and wholesale power market rules
  • Effective at triaging and prioritizing across a wide range of tasks and project managing cross-functional tasks to completion
  • An excellent communicator (including to engineers and other non-lawyers) focused on solutions and willing to explain the “why” behind legal advice
  • Substantively agile: someone who enjoys leaning into new areas, and is comfortable learning new things (and learning quickly!)
  • Detail-oriented while moving lightning fast
  • Passionate about clean energy and making advanced fission a reality
  • An optimist at heart
  • Resourceful, inquisitive, and willing and able to learn quickly
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA. This role will also likely need to travel occasionally to our project sites, which include locations in Idaho, Ohio, Tennessee, and Texas.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $230,000-$250,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

Position Description

Core Design Engineers at Oklo are responsible for designing performant and manufacturable reactor cores which balance neutronic, thermal hydraulic, material, mechanical, and economic considerations. Work performed by Core Design Engineers includes executing multiphysics simulations to assess core performance, writing clear and thorough design documentation, performing analyses to validate and verify core requirements, and working closely with fabrication engineers to mature their designs.

Core design is an interdisciplinary field, we are looking for applicants who have a holistic understanding of reactor physics that lets them quickly ascertain how proposed design changes will impact core performance. Level will be determined based on applicant experience.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Traveling to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) 2x per calendar quarter for team meetings, company offsite, or other business gatherings

  • Translating top-level stakeholder requirements into well-written system functional requirements

  • Documenting work using modern tools and techniques, and producing well-written technical reports

  • Collaborating cross-functionally to define performance requirements, and providing technical feedback to methods development teams

  • Bachelors, Masters, or PhD in nuclear engineering or a related field

title: Cost Accountant
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Cost Accountant to join our team.

Position Description

The Cost Accountant will play a key role in Oklo's accounting function, with primary responsibility over cost identification and coding for Oklo’s capital project spend, including for plant and inventory workstreams. This role partners closely with project controllers, procurement, accounts payable, and other stakeholders to make appropriate GAAP accounting conclusions for spend, including for capitalization and GL allocation of plant and fixed asset costs. The Cost Accountant will execute internal controls supporting Oklo's SOX environment, assist internal and external auditors, and deliver accurate monthly and quarterly close schedules. The ability to apply accounting policy consistently, investigate variances, and stay organized across a growing asset base will be a critical success factor.

A second critical aspect of this role will be managing and overseeing the Company's fixed assets register. This role will maintain the register and ensure assets are accurately classified, supported, and placed in service on a timely basis. The Cost Accountant will also run monthly depreciation, prepare related journal entries and roll-forwards, and reconcile the fixed asset subledger to the general ledger as part of the month-end close.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Partner with project controllers, procurement, accounts payable, and other stakeholders to review project spend for proper capitalization treatment under company policy.
  • Maintain complete supporting documentation for capitalization conclusions, asset records, depreciation, and disposals in accordance with accounting policy and internal controls
  • Support internal and external audits by providing fixed asset schedules, transaction support, control evidence, and timely responses to inquiries
  • Partner with project controllers, procurement, and accounts payable to confirm asset descriptions, ownership, location, useful life, cost center, and placed-in-service status
  • Align with project team for single source of truth related to capital project portfolio reporting as empowering projects teams to focus on progressing their projects
  • Manage the capital project lifecycle, including additions, transfers, placed-in-service dates, disposals, retirements, and other changes to the fixed asset register
  • Monitor construction-in-progress balances and coordinate the timely transfer of completed projects into the appropriate fixed asset categories
  • Run monthly depreciation, validate system calculations, and prepare or post the related journal entries as part of the month-end close
  • Reconcile the fixed asset subledger to the general ledger each month and research and resolve reconciling items promptly
  • Prepare fixed asset journal entries for additions, transfers, disposals, impairments, reclassifications, and other required adjustments
  • Prepare monthly and quarterly fixed asset roll-forwards, capital expenditure schedules, and related financial reporting support
  • Coordinate periodic physical inventories and asset verification procedures and investigate identified discrepancies
  • Identify opportunities to improve and automate fixed asset accounting, capitalization review, reconciliation, and reporting processes
  • Support other accounting responsibilities and special projects as assigned as the Company's operations and asset base continue to grow

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a related field
  • 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including fixed asset or cost accounting responsibilities
  • Experience managing fixed asset additions, depreciation, disposals, reconciliations, and capitalization assessments
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, fixed asset accounting principles, and Microsoft Excel

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience using NetSuite and NetAsset fixed asset management software
  • Experience using Zip
  • CPA or CMA is a plus
  • Master’s degree in accountancy
  • Fast growth startup or public company experience

Competencies

We are looking for someone that is:

  • Analytical - reviews transaction detail, identifies capitalization indicators, and explains changes in fixed asset balances
  • Policy oriented - applies the Company's capitalization policy and U.S. GAAP consistently and documents conclusions clearly

title: Deployment Project Manager
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Deployment Project Manager to join our team.

Position Description

The Deployment Project Manager is a pivotal, execution-focused role responsible for advancing Oklo’s mission to deliver clean, affordable, and reliable energy. This individual owns the end-to-end delivery of one or more highly complex powerhouse projects, from design integration and site development through construction, startup, commissioning, and turnover to operations.

These multi-year, non-recurring projects include significant first-of-a-kind scope, substantial commercial value, evolving risks, and complex dependencies across internal teams, external partners, regulators, and other key stakeholders. The Deployment Project Manager serves as the central point of coordination, driving integrated planning, decision-making, risk management, and clear communication among project teams, executive leadership, and external parties. Success in this role requires a strategic and hands-on leader with a startup mindset - someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, operate effectively in a resource-constrained environment, and maintain momentum, accountability, and alignment throughout the full project lifecycle.

Location: Remote, with 25%–40% travel required

  • Lead end-to-end execution of powerhouse facility deployments from design through startup and turnover to operations.
  • Support and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, milestones, and execution tools to monitor progress and drive delivery.
  • Identify, manage, and escalate risks, issues, dependencies, and changes to protect critical path, licensing, regulatory, and commercial objectives.
  • Lead project governance routines, including status reviews, stage-gate reviews, and executive reporting.
  • Manage project scope, risks, issues, and dependencies while proactively identifying and implementing mitigation strategies.
  • Communicate project status, recommendations, and strategic insights to stakeholders ranging from project teams to executive leadership.

  • Serve as the primary point of coordination among internal teams, customers, contractors, vendors, and other external stakeholders.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

title: Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls
description:

Position Description

Oklo Isotopes is building scalable U.S. radioisotope production capabilities in facilities dedicated to producing essential isotopes for healthcare, space, industry, research, and defense applications. Oklo’s isotope operations include the production and processing of medically and industrially important radioisotopes using advanced radiochemical processes, hot cells, gloveboxes, and specialized nuclear facilities.

We are seeking a Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) to lead the radiochemistry and CMC organization supporting Oklo’s isotope production programs, initially focused on Lu-177 production and Am-241 and Ra-226 processing for medical, industrial, and other applications.

The Director will lead radiochemical process development and control, technology transfer, analytical strategy, process optimization, troubleshooting, validation support, and process lifecycle management, while building and managing a multidisciplinary radiochemistry team.

The successful candidate will develop rigorous, scalable processes from development through commissioning and routine manufacturing. The role requires deep radiochemistry and isotope-processing expertise, strong technical and team leadership, and experience in nuclear, radiological, quality, and cGMP environments.

The Director will collaborate across Manufacturing, Facility Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Radiation Safety, Engineering, and Supply Chain to establish safe, compliant, reliable, and scalable isotope production.

This is a on-site position located in Austin, Texas.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Lead the CMC and radiochemistry organization for isotope process development, implementation, technical support, and lifecycle management.

  • Establish the technical basis for manufacturing processes, including process flows, material balances, critical parameters, operating ranges, specifications, and controls.
  • Lead development, scale-up, optimization, and implementation of radiochemical processes in hot cells, gloveboxes, and laboratory or remote systems.

  • Build, mentor, and manage the radiochemistry team; establish technical standards, procedures, training, and documentation; and promote safety, quality, rigor, and operational excellence.
  • Support regulatory activities, audits, inspections, and development of new isotope products, processes, technologies, and capabilities.

  • Masters in Radiochemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.

  • Experience with CMC development, process characterization, technology transfer, process validation, continued process verification, and manufacturing science and technology (MS&T).

title: Director of Manufacturing Strategy
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Director of Manufacturing Strategy to join our team.

Position Description

The Director of Manufacturing Strategy will define and continuously refine how Oklo converts ambitious product and deployment plans into an executable manufacturing system. Reporting to the Head of Supply Chain, this leader will integrate engineering judgment, supplier-market intelligence, commercial inputs, and strategic analysis to help Oklo achieve aggressive lead-time, cost, quality, and scalability goals.

During Oklo's first-of-a-kind (FOAK) build, the Director will work directly with Responsible Engineers and suppliers to develop and improve component-level manufacturing strategies, resolve industrialization challenges, and assess whether supplier processes can produce conforming hardware at the required rate. The role will translate these findings into company-wide make-vs-buy recommendations and manufacturing roadmaps.

This is a hybrid technical and commercial strategy role. It requires enough manufacturing depth to evaluate processes, tooling, qualification needs, quality controls, production constraints, and recovery plans, as well as enough commercial fluency to compare market options and support scenario modeling. The role partners closely with Engineering, Procurement, Strategy, Quality, Program Management, and Oklo's internal fabrication leadership.

This role develops the strategy for how Oklo will manufacture at scale; it does not establish, manage, or operate factories. When Oklo elects to make a product internally, execution transitions to the internal fabrication organization. Procurement retains ownership of supplier commercial strategy, sourcing, negotiations, and contracting.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Own Oklo's enterprise manufacturing strategy, connecting product and deployment plans to executable manufacturing pathways across external suppliers and internal fabrication.
  • Lead cross-functional make-vs-buy analyses and recommendations using technical feasibility, supplier capability and capacity, lead time, cost, quality, schedule risk, capital requirements, intellectual property, and long-term scalability.
  • Build decision frameworks and provide supply-market intelligence to the Strategy team so alternative manufacturing scenarios can be modeled with credible assumptions and sensitivities.
  • Partner with Responsible Engineers during FOAK execution to define supplier manufacturing strategies, review process plans, identify manufacturability risks, and improve the likelihood of delivering conforming hardware on schedule.
  • Assess suppliers' manufacturing processes, equipment, workforce, quality systems, special-process controls, qualification paths, current loading, surge capacity, and ability to meet Oklo's forecast production rates.
  • Translate supplier assessments into actionable technical recommendations for Engineering and clear capability guidance for Procurement, while preserving Procurement's ownership of commercial negotiations, contracts, and supplier relationships.
  • Identify critical manufacturing constraints and fragile supply-chain nodes; develop mitigation options such as alternate processes, supplier development plans, second sources, design changes, phased capacity investments, or selective insourcing.
  • Support technical vetting and due diligence of potential suppliers alongside Engineering, Quality, and Procurement, including site visits, process reviews, readiness assessments, and production-rate validation.
  • Develop industrialization and manufacturing-readiness roadmaps that bridge FOAK builds to repeatable production, including learning-curve assumptions, yield and throughput improvement, tooling, automation, qualification, and capacity ramps.
  • Establish and track manufacturing-strategy metrics and decision milestones related to lead time, cost, quality, capacity, scalability, risk retirement, and make-vs-buy outcomes.
  • Provide leadership with concise recommendations, trade studies, and portfolio-level views of manufacturing readiness, constraints, and investment choices.
  • Create reusable standards, playbooks, and lessons learned that strengthen manufacturing planning across programs without adding unnecessary process

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical, manufacturing, industrial, materials, aerospace, nuclear, or a closely related engineering discipline.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering, industrialization, production engineering, supplier manufacturing, operations strategy, or a related hardware-manufacturing field, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated ability to understand and evaluate manufacturing processes, process capability, tooling, qualification, yield, cycle time, throughput, capacity, quality controls, and production risk.
  • Experience supporting complex, low-volume or FOAK hardware through supplier selection, development, qualification, and transition toward repeatable production.
  • Experience leading make-vs-buy, manufacturing-footprint, capacity, cost, or industrialization analyses with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Ability to combine incomplete technical, commercial, and schedule information into practical recommendations and clearly state assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and decision points.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with Responsible Engineers, suppliers, procurement professionals, executives, and program leaders.
  • Willingness to travel to supplier sites, manufacturing locations, and Oklo headquarters as business needs require.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Master of Business Administration (MBA), master's degree in engineering, or equivalent commercial, finance, corporate strategy, or business-development experience.
  • Experience in nuclear energy, aerospace, defense, semiconductors, energy systems, advanced industrial equipment, or another highly regulated hardware environment.
  • Direct experience across both technical manufacturing and commercial or strategic decision-making, including should-cost analysis, total-cost modeling, capacity investment cases, or supplier business assessments.
  • Experience with fabrication and special processes such as machining, welding, forming, casting, forging, additive manufacturing, heat treatment, coatings, nondestructive examination, or complex assembly.
  • Experience scaling from prototype or FOAK builds into low-rate initial production and higher-rate manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with nuclear-quality, export-control, or other regulated supply-chain requirements.

Competencies

  • Strategic and technically grounded: Connects manufacturing details to enterprise choices without losing sight of what must happen on the shop floor.
  • Commercially fluent: Understands that supplier capability, price, lead time, investment, risk, and incentives must be evaluated together.

description:

Position Description

The Director of Market Analytics is the intelligence engine of Oklo's Origination organization. You will own the market research, energy price forecasting, load growth analysis, and competitive intelligence that underpin every site selection decision, offtake negotiation, and project finance model in Oklo's Aurora powerhouse pipeline. You report to the Sr Director of Origination and work in close partnership with the Directors of Land & Real Estate, as well as Oklo's Finance team on revenue model inputs.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Market Research & Forecasting

  • Own Oklo's long-term power market forecasting function across all target geographies: capacity prices, energy prices, ancillary services, and carbon compliance costs
  • Develop and maintain market models covering AI datacenter load growth, electrification, generation retirements, new build pipeline, and transmission constraints
  • Produce market assessments supporting site selection, development prioritization, and go/no-go decisions
  • Monitor and analyze ISO/RTO capacity market results, energy market dynamics, and grid planning studies

Commercial & Policy Intelligence

  • Provide market intelligence to support PPA negotiations: pricing benchmarks, contract structure norms, and counterparty credit analysis
  • Track federal and state energy policy: IRA Section 45U PTC, state clean energy standards, carbon markets, and capacity market rules
  • Monitor FERC rulemaking and RTO/ISO market design changes affecting Aurora powerhouse siting and interconnection economics
  • Produce quarterly market intelligence briefings for the VP of Origination, VP of Development, and board

Offtake Structure & Value Optimization

  • Lead comparative analysis of Oklo’s power offtake structures to maximize company value across the development portfolio, evaluating: Build-Own-Transfer (BOT) arrangements with utilities or sovereign buyers; physical bilateral PPAs with corporate, utility, and government counterparties; Virtual PPAs (VPPAs) and financial contracts for difference (CfD) with creditworthy corporate offtakers; capacity market participation and merchant revenue strategies for unsold output; and hybrid structures combining elements of the above to optimize risk-adjusted project returns
  • Develop and maintain a quantitative offtake structure comparison model evaluating each structure across: NPV to Oklo, project finance bankability, revenue certainty vs. upside optionality, counterparty credit risk, regulatory complexity, and balance sheet impact — enabling the VP of Origination and CFO to make data-driven offtake strategy decisions at the project and portfolio level
  • Produce deal-specific offtake structure recommendations for each Aurora powerhouse project, factoring in local market conditions, offtaker creditworthiness, state regulatory environment, IRA 45U PTC monetization strategy, and Oklo’s portfolio-level risk exposure

title: General Internship Application 2027
location_raw: Santa Clara, CA or Any Office Location
description:
We are excited to announce an open call for talented interns to join Oklo's dynamic team! Below are multiple positions across various disciplines that may be available, offering the chance to work on innovative projects for Summer 2027. If you're passionate about solving complex challenges, thrive in a collaborative environment, and are eager to contribute to groundbreaking solutions, we encourage you to apply.

Requirements

Oklo interns are required to:

  • Relocate or be available to work out of Santa Clara CA where Oklo Headquarters is located for the duration of the internship or out of one of our satellite locations in Denver, CO, Brooklyn, NY, Idaho Falls, ID, or Washington D.C.
  • Be available to work 30-40 hours per week between June 7, 2027 - August 20, 2027 (depending on the scope of work)
  • Be currently enrolled or recently (2027) graduated with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree from an accredited university

Intern Position Descriptions

Core Thermal Hydraulics Intern

The CTH Intern will develop intermediate fidelity (IF) subchannel and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for applications in sodium fast reactors (SFRs). The project will involve comparisons between simulation results and experimental data. The exact topic will depend on interest and company needs but could cover fluid-structure interaction, turbulence model development, uncertainty quantification, or surrogate modeling.

  • Required Qualifications
    • Coursework in fluid mechanics and heat transfer
    • Experience with 3-D CFD and meshing workflows
    • Proficiency in Python
    • Clear technical communication and documentation skills
  • Bonus Qualifications
    • Experience with advanced 3-D CFD concepts (large eddy simulation, fluid-structure interaction)
    • Familiarity with high-performance computing workflows and tools
    • Experience with MOOSE
    • Familiarity with statistics and reduced order modeling

Materials Intern

Working with members of Oklo’s Materials Team, will help with the selection and qualification of materials for use in nuclear reactor systems. Typical work duties include computational model development and implementation, engineering analysis, documentation, and interfacing with our fuel fabrication and engineering teams.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Analyzing material performance across expected operating conditions
    • Developing new analysis methods to predict material behavior in service
    • Performing engineering analyses, including assessments of thermal performance, mechanical performance, safety performance, manufacturability, and cost.
    • Collaborating cross-functionally to provide technical feedback to quick-iterating computational teams.
    • Authoring technical reports using modern documentation tools and techniques
  • Required Qualifications
    • Experience working with and developing material behavior models
    • Experience with material characterization (material testing, metallography)
    • Background in nuclear, chemical, materials engineering, or equivalent
    • Motivated learner who is adept at efficiently summarizing literature
  • Bonus Qualifications
    • Experience with engineering simulation software, such as ANSYS or COMSOL
    • Coding or data analysis experience (e.g., Python or similar tools)

Mechanical Analyst Intern

This intern will contribute to the evaluation and optimization of mechanical components that are critical to Oklo’s advanced power plant designs. This position offers hands-on experience in applying engineering fundamentals, performing structural analysis, and integrating results into design iterations.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Apply first-principles mechanics and strength of materials to support analysis of structural components
    • Assist in summarizing mechanical analysis results for design teams, highlighting key findings such as peak stresses, margins of safety, and potential design revisions
    • Support the development of technical documentation, ensuring clear and concise communication of assumptions, methods, and results
    • Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and testing teams to help inform design improvements
  • Required Qualifications
    • Working toward a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline
    • Strong foundation in mechanics of materials, dynamics, and heat transfer
    • Exposure to FEA tools (e.g., Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL, or similar) through coursework or projects
    • Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or another programming language for basic data analysis or workflow automation
    • Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly document and present technical findings
  • Bonus Qualifications
    • Prior research or project experience involving creep, fatigue, or thermal-mechanical problems
    • Familiarity with engineering codes and standards (e.g., ASME, AISC, or similar)
    • Experience using Git or another version control system

Instrumentation and Controls Intern

This intern will contribute to the development, integration, and testing of measurement and control systems that support advanced reactor operation and power generation. This position provides hands-on exposure to sensors, automation, and control strategies, while giving interns the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Assist in developing and testing sensors, instrumentation, and actuators under real design constraints
    • Help design and implement control algorithms for equipment and processes
    • Support the integration of I&C components into reactor systems and analysis workflows
    • Contribute to documenting methods, results, and system designs in a clear and professional manner
    • Collaborate with design and analysis teams to provide feedback that supports rapid iteration and improvement
  • Required Qualifications
    • Working toward a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
    • Familiarity with measurement techniques, data acquisition, and signal processing
    • Exposure to control theory and feedback systems through coursework or projects
    • Basic programming skills in Python (or similar) for data analysis and automation
    • Strong communication skills and an eagerness to learn in a collaborative environment
  • Bonus Qualifications
    • Experience with circuit design (analog or digital) from labs, research, or projects
    • Exposure to communication protocols and digital networks
    • Familiarity with Git version control

Neutronics Methodologies Intern

This intern will assist in updating and streamlining neutronic methodologies to align with the latest format and standards. They will ensure that the methodologies match the way the code base builds the model, verifying consistency across both. This position also involves identifying and documenting gaps or discrepancies in the review process for future improvements.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Update and optimize neutronic methodologies to the latest format and standards.
    • Ensure methodologies align with the way the code base builds the model.
    • Identify and document any gaps or discrepancies in the current processes.
    • Collaborate with team members to ensure consistency and accuracy in modeling procedures.
  • Required Qualifications
    • Proficient in Python for scripting and automation.
    • Familiar with AsciiDoc for documentation and formatting.
    • Strong background in nuclear engineering and neutronics.
    • Attention to detail with an ability to identify gaps in methodologies and processes.

Process Intern

This intern will support the design and analysis of fluid and power systems that are essential to Oklo’s advanced reactors. This position provides hands-on experience with system modeling, equipment evaluation, and prototyping, offering interns a chance to apply classroom knowledge to real-world energy systems.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Assist in designing fluid and process systems, including piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and heat exchangers
    • Support definition of process equipment specifications, performance criteria, and operating conditions
    • Contribute to prototype setup and testing activities for iterative system design and validation
    • Help prepare technical documentation to support system layout, fabrication, installation, and operation
    • Collaborate with engineers on analyses to evaluate performance and inform design refinements
    • Document results and methods in a clear and professional manner for use across design and regulatory teams
  • Required Qualifications
    • Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline
    • Background in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer through coursework or projects
    • Familiarity with process or system modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, Aspen, or similar)
    • Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail
    • Ability to clearly communicate technical findings through reports or presentations
  • Bonus Qualifications
    • Experience with lab work, prototyping, or experimental systems
    • Exposure to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) or process design coursework
    • Familiarity with pumps, heat exchangers, or thermal-fluid systems from research or internships

Prototyping/Manufacturing Intern

The prototyping engineering intern will be a part of the prototyping and visualization team.

  • Key Responsibilities
    • Assist in machining and general fabrication of prototypes and test setups
    • Work with engineers to develop and execute testing procedures for mechanical systems
    • Support assembly, troubleshooting, and optimization of electro-mechanical systems
    • Conduct inspections and quality control on fabricated components
    • Document test results, process improvements, and technical findings
    • Collaborate with the engineering team to improve designs and manufacturing processes
    • Maintain a safe and organized workspace
  • Required qualifications
    • Mechanical, manufacturing, electrical, nuclear, chemical, or similar engineering student graduating with bachelors, masters, or PhD within the following year
    • Hands-on experience with mechanical fabrication, machining, or assembly
    • Good understanding of mechanical design, materials, and manufacturing processes
    • Familiarity with mechanical measurement tools (calipers, micrometers, etc.)
    • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and schematics
    • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently and in a team environment
    • Good communication and technical documentation skills
  • Bonus qualifications
    • Experience with manual or CNC machining
    • Exposure to electronics, sensors, and control systems (mechatronics experience)
    • Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or similar)
    • Experience with welding, 3D printing, or other prototyping techniques
    • Understanding of fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, or materials science
    • Experience with data acquisition systems and programming (Python, LabVIEW, or MATLAB)

This role is ideal for someone looking to grow their operational skill set in core business operational functions and is passionate about contributing to initiatives that drive efficiency while supporting key compliance functions across the organization.

title: General Open Call for Applications
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are excited to announce a General Open Call for Applications, open to all applicants who possess a passion for excellence and a drive to make a positive impact. We are searching for exceptional individuals who can bring diverse perspectives and talents to our organization. To apply, please submit your resume and a cover letter to the provided email address or through our online application portal.

NOTE: Due to the nature of this open call, not all positions may be available immediately. However, we will regularly review applications and reach out to qualified individuals as suitable opportunities arise. Your application will be carefully considered for future roles that align with your skills and aspirations

Competencies

We are looking for people who are:

  • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality
  • Willing and able to learn quickly
  • Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us
  • Willing to think differently and do things in new ways
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment
  • Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before
  • Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems
  • An excellent writer who can write in modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is a clear, efficient, and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • While specific experience is not a mandatory requirement, a demonstrated track record of excellence in any field will be highly regarded. Tell us how you want to contribute to our team and mission!
  • We encourage candidates from all backgrounds and experience levels to apply.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation:

  • Oklo offers competitive compensation packages. Compensation is generally based on the candidates experience level and expertise.
  • Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

title: Hot Cell Design Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a radiological Hot Cell Design Engineer to join our dynamic fuel recycling engineering group, which is designing and deploying a modern nuclear fuel recycling facility. This is a rare opportunity to contribute to the design and development of one of the most advanced radiological hot cell systems ever.

Position Description:

As a Hot Cell Design Engineer at Oklo, you will help shape a highly specialized, remotely-operable hot cell environment that enables the safe, efficient processing of used nuclear fuel (UNF).

You’ll work collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team of mechanical, nuclear, chemical, and controls engineers to integrate critical systems such as shielding, containment, and remote operations into an industrial-scale recycling facility.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead or support the mechanical and systems design of radiological hot cells used in UNF recycling, including shielding, ventilation, confinement, and remote handling systems

  • Define equipment and material layouts, including material transfer pathways and maintenance access strategies

  • Work with radiation modeling and safety analysis specialists to develop shielding requirements and establish design constraints

  • Integrate robotic and remote handling technologies (e.g., manipulators, cameras, cranes, etc.) into cell design

  • Contribute to the structural evaluation of confinement systems, ensuring compliance with fire protection, external hazard, and natural phenomena hazard requirements

  • Collaborate with structural, HVAC, instrumentation, and process engineers to ensure seamless integration across all hot cell systems

  • Participate in Failure Modes and Effects Analyses (FMEA), hazard analyses, and radiological safety assessments

  • Contribute to design reviews, procurement specifications, and installation and commissioning plans

  • Support prototyping, testing, and commissioning of hot cell subsystems

Competencies:

We are looking for a Hot Cell Design Engineer that is:

  • Passionate about clean energy, fuel recycling, and efficient stewardship of natural resources

  • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

  • Willing and able to learn quickly

  • Willing to think differently and do things in new ways

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly-iterative startup environment

  • Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving while not leaning only on what has been done before

  • Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems

  • An excellent writer who can write in a modern active voice (so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!)

  • Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline

  • 5+ years of experience in radiological facility design, glovebox or hot cell engineering, or radiological material handling

  • Strong working knowledge of remote handling systems, robotics, or manipulator technologies

  • Understanding of radiation shielding principles, criticality safety, and radiological protection standards

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate on cross-functional teams and integrate feedback from engineering, licensing, and safety

  • Strong systems engineering intuition and problem-solving capabilities

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience with hot cells used in nuclear fuel cycle facilities, isotope production, or defense applications

title: Instrumentation & Controls Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for an Instrumentation & Controls Engineer to join our team in Idaho Falls.

Position Description

Oklo is transforming the future of energy, and we are looking for an experienced Instrumentation & Controls Engineer to lead and support the design, integration, commissioning, and operation of instrumentation and control systems for test platforms used in advanced nuclear technology development.

In this role, you will translate test and process requirements into reliable measurement, control, data-acquisition, and protective functions. You will work closely with test, process, mechanical, electrical, software, quality, and operations personnel throughout the full system lifecycle, from concept development and equipment selection through fabrication, testing, startup, troubleshooting, and configuration management with travel up to 10%.

The ideal candidate combines strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on field experience and broad knowledge of industrial instrumentation. Strong familiarity with the Emerson DeltaV distributed control system is preferred. Experience working under a nuclear quality assurance program, particularly ASME NQA-1, is also preferred.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • I&C System Design and Architecture: Develop control-system architectures, functional requirements, I/O strategies, network concepts, and interfaces for test platforms and supporting facility systems.
  • Instrumentation Engineering: Select and specify instruments for temperature, pressure, flow, level, position, force, strain, vibration, and other process or test measurements. Evaluate accuracy, range, response time, environmental suitability, installation requirements, and measurement uncertainty.
  • Control System Development: Develop, configure, and verify control logic, control modules, operator graphics, alarms, interlocks, permissives, sequences, and data-acquisition functions using distributed control systems, programmable logic controllers, and related platforms. Able to develop new system architecture.
  • Engineering Documentation: Prepare and maintain I/O lists, instrument indexes, data sheets, loop diagrams, wiring diagrams, control narratives, logic diagrams, network drawings, alarm setpoint documentation, test procedures, and as-built records.
  • Test Platform Integration: Coordinate the integration of instruments, control panels, remote I/O, analyzers, control valves, electrical interfaces, industrial networks, and data systems with mechanical and process equipment.
  • Commissioning and Verification: Develop and execute design-verification activities, factory and site acceptance tests, loop checks, functional tests, calibration reviews, control-system checkout, and startup plans.
  • Test Operations and Troubleshooting: Support test readiness reviews and test execution. Diagnose instrumentation, controls, electrical, communications, software, and data-acquisition issues, perform root-cause investigations, and implement technically sound corrective actions.
  • Procurement and Supplier Oversight: Develop technical specifications, evaluate vendor proposals, review supplier submittals, support procurement, and verify that equipment and services meet technical and quality requirements.
  • Design and Configuration Control: Manage design changes, software and hardware configurations, setpoints, drawings, calculations, and technical records in accordance with applicable engineering and quality requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, nuclear engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Experience designing, specifying, procuring, commissioning, or troubleshooting process and mechanical equipment.
  • Experience preparing or reviewing piping and instrumentation diagrams, process-flow diagrams, equipment data sheets, engineering calculations, technical specifications, and vendor drawings.
  • Working knowledge of pumps, valves, piping, heat exchangers, tanks, pressure equipment, heaters, or similar process components.
  • Ability to perform fluid-flow, pressure-drop, heat-transfer, and equipment-sizing calculations.
  • Ability to lift, move, and position equipment weighing up to 30 pounds.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Strong familiarity with the Emerson DeltaV distributed control system, including system architecture, controllers, I/O, configuration, graphics, alarms, control modules, batch or sequence functions, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience designing or supporting thermal-hydraulic, mechanical, chemical, high-temperature, high-pressure, or liquid-metal test systems.
  • Experience working in nuclear, aerospace, defense, pharmaceutical, chemical processing, power generation, or another highly regulated industry.
  • Familiarity with functional safety, safety instrumented systems, alarm management, or control-system cybersecurity practices.
  • Familiarity with ASME NQA-1 requirements, particularly requirements related to design control, software control, test control, calibration, procurement, document control, and configuration management.
  • Professional Engineer licensure, Engineer-in-Training certification, or relevant controls or automation certification.

Competencies

  • Instrumentation and Controls Engineering: Strong understanding of industrial measurement, process control, control-system architecture, signal conditioning, data acquisition, and equipment integration.
  • Control System Knowledge: Practical experience with distributed control systems, programmable logic controllers, human-machine interfaces, alarm management, control loops, industrial networks, and test-control hardware.
  • Practical Engineering Judgment: Ability to develop systems that can be fabricated, installed, calibrated, operated, maintained, and modified safely and effectively.
  • Analytical and Detail-Oriented: Able to evaluate system behavior, identify failure modes, resolve technical issues, and maintain accurate engineering and configuration records.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Able to clearly communicate requirements, design decisions, risks, and operating conditions to engineers, technicians, suppliers, quality personnel, and test operators.
  • Process Development: Able to develop and author process and procedure guidance for testing programs and operations.
  • Adaptability: Comfortable working in a fast-paced development environment where priorities, system configurations, and test requirements may evolve.

title: Mechanical Design Engineer - Core Mechanical Design
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Core Mechanical Design Engineer to join our engineering team.

Position Description

As a Core Mechanical Design Engineer, you will be responsible for designing core assemblies and components that will be used in our advanced reactors. You will take designs through our process from conceptual to final design. During this design lifecycle, you will be responsible for working with Oklo’s Fuel Fabrication team to refine the design for improved manufacturability and inspectability. Additionally, you will responsible for creating other documentation to support the definition of these components, including but not limited to, drawings, product and material specifications, design basis documents, and calculation documents.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Develop the design of these components to satisfy both performance and manufacturing requirements
  • Create and develop design documentation to define requirements
  • Conduct and participate in design reviews, providing and receiving technical feedback
  • Rigorously evaluate mechanical designs to identify deficiencies and proactively propose and implement solutions
  • Generate and maintain detailed 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and bills of materials using controlled processes in PDM/PLM systems
  • Coordinate closely with analysis teams to guide and interpret thermal, structural, fatigue, and safety analyses in support of design validation
  • Perform detailed manufacturability reviews, tolerance studies, and DFM/DFA assessments to prepare components for fabrication and assembly
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of Oklo’s mechanical design processes, tools, and standards through feedback and development of best practices

Experience Level:

  • 3-10 years of industry experience in mechanical or structural design within sectors such as aerospace, automotive, energy, or industrial equipment

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or higher degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline
  • Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling software (e.g., Siemens NX, CATIA, SolidWorks), including part modeling, large assemblies, and detailed drawings
  • Experience with CAD version control using PDM/PLM tools (e.g., Teamcenter, SolidWorks PDM, Windchill)
  • Solid understanding of mechanical design principles, including DFM (Design for Manufacturability), DFA (Design for Assembly), and tolerance stack-up analysis
  • Ability to apply GD&T per ASME Y14.5-2018 (or other similar standard) to engineering drawings
  • Working knowledge of material selection (particularly metals), manufacturing methods, and fabrication techniques
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate on cross-functional teams, integrating feedback from analysis, manufacturing, and systems engineering
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document and present engineering work
  • Comfortable working with external manufacturers and engineering consultants for fabrication and analysis support

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Background in designing components for high-integrity or safety-critical systems (e.g., nuclear, aerospace, defense, or heavy industry)
  • Proven ability to lead hardware projects through the full development cycle—from concept and design to testing and production
  • Comfortable working with manufacturers and engineering consultants for fabrication and analysis support
  • Knowledge of manufacturing and inspection processes
  • Experience with precision machine design and tolerancing
  • Understanding of thermal-mechanical analysis principles, with experience designing for high-temperature environments
  • Basic knowledge of nuclear fission and radiation effects on materials and components
  • Exposure to simulation tools (e.g., ANSYS) and scripting languages (e.g., Python) is a plus
  • ASME GD&T Professional certification (Senior or Technologist Level) is a plus
  • Proficiency with SolidWorks software is a plus

Competencies

We are looking for a Core Mechanical Design Engineer that is:

  • Competent in 3D modeling software and has a solid understanding of mechanical design principals
  • An experienced team player who can work effectively across both internal resources and external suppliers
  • Passionate about clean energy
  • An optimist at heart
  • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

title: Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer to join our Operations Engineering team.

Position Description

The Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer supports the planning, coordination, and field execution of commissioning and startup activities for Oklo facilities. This role helps transition systems and facilities from construction through testing, turnover, operational readiness, initial operation, and project completion. This role works directly with Operations, Engineering, Construction, Maintenance, Quality, Safety, vendors, contractors, and other project organizations to ensure systems are properly scoped, tested, documented, accepted, and ready for operation. This engineer develops and reviews commissioning plans, test procedures, system turnover requirements, schedules, resource needs, and readiness criteria and then provides onsite engineering support during execution.

During field assignments, the Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer may serve as a system-based commissioning engineer, test engineer, shift test engineer, or field engineering lead. The engineer confirms system and test readiness, supports test teams, monitors plant response and test data, coordinates troubleshooting, resolves deficiencies, and ensures results are properly evaluated and documented.

This is a project-deployment role with remote work between field assignments. When assigned to an active commissioning or startup project, the Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer must be prepared to mobilize to the applicable project site for periods lasting several weeks to several months. Upon completion of an assignment, the engineer may return to remote work until mobilized for the next project. The frequency, location, and duration of assignments will vary based on company and project needs.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Develop and implement commissioning and startup plans, strategies, schedules, system-based work scopes, and execution methods
  • Define commissioning boundaries, test objectives, prerequisites, acceptance criteria, required resources, and system turnover requirements
  • Develop, review, verify, and maintain preoperational, commissioning, integrated, and startup test procedures
  • Translate design requirements, safety requirements, specifications, calculations, vendor information, and system requirements into executable test methods and acceptance criteria
  • Develop and maintain commissioning test matrices, requirements-traceability tools, system status records, turnover packages, and test completion documentation
  • Support systemization and define the structures, systems, components, boundaries, and work packages needed for effective commissioning and turnover
  • Coordinate construction completion, system walkdowns, punch-list resolution, turnover documentation, and acceptance of systems for testing
  • Verify test prerequisites, plant configuration, test boundaries, equipment status, temporary configurations, instrumentation, personnel, and procedural readiness before test execution
  • Participate in pre-job briefs, daily coordination meetings, shift turnovers, schedule reviews, and test-readiness reviews
  • Provide field engineering oversight during commissioning and startup testing
  • Monitor system response and test data in real time and compare observed performance against expected results and acceptance criteria
  • Support operators and test directors during system manipulations, integrated testing, startup testing, and other significant plant evolutions

We are seeking a strategic, analytical, and systems-minded Portfolio Planner to translate Oklo's project portfolio into an integrated organizational resource and staffing plan. The Portfolio Planner will work with project teams and department leaders to convert the portfolio roadmap into forward-looking capacity requirements, identify resource constraints, and inform the timing and mix of internal hiring, redeployment, and external support. The role will maintain a portfolio-wide view while Project Schedulers remain accountable for detailed project-level schedule development and status.

Over time, this role will help develop management accounting frameworks that improve visibility into internal resource utilization, total project cost, and the value created by internal teams. This work will support operating decisions, capital planning, project benchmarking, and increasingly rigorous internal and externally funded project reporting.

This role will partner closely with Project Budgeting and Controls, project teams, functional leaders, Finance, Accounting, and People Operations. The role reports into the Sr. Director of Project Budgeting and Controls.

Establish and continuously improve proxy-based demand curves using factors such as project type, total project value, design maturity, regulatory pathway, execution strategy, complexity, and delivery stage.

title: Probabilistic Risk Assessment Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) Engineer to join our team.

Position Description

The Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) Engineer is responsible for conducting probabilistic risk analyses to support our fast reactor design development, licensing, deployment, and operation. PRA Engineers work with our engineering teams to conduct quantitative risk analyses, including identification of initiating events (via hazards evaluation approaches such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEAs)), development of event trees and fault trees, quantification of event sequence probabilities, and evaluation of event sequence consequences. PRA Engineers also work with our engineering design teams to incorporate risk insights back into the design to drive improvements in reliability and safety.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Developing probabilistic risk analysis models of our fast reactor designs
  • Working with our engineering analysis teams to analyze event sequences and compile risk insights
  • Using PRA techniques to evaluate external hazards
  • Working with our engineering design teams to incorporate risk insights into the design and improve system reliability
  • Supporting licensing activities through generation of technical reports, technical analyses, and supporting documentation

Minimum Qualifications:

  • At least 5 years of work experience
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or similar
  • Familiarity with PRA techniques

  • Experience with fast reactor design and analysis

The Project Scheduler will partner closely with the Project Manager, Project Controller, Project Sponsor, functional leads, and external vendors to establish executable plans, identify critical and near-critical paths, evaluate schedule impacts, and support timely recovery decisions. This role interfaces directly with EPCs and other vendors to integrate external schedules, validate progress, and hold schedule contributors accountable for timely and high-quality status information. The Project Scheduler will work in close coordination with the Portfolio Planner to apply common schedule coding, calendars, milestone definitions, and quality standards. Support baseline establishment and controlled re-baselining in accordance with governance requirements.

  • Critical Path and Risk Analysis: Analyze critical and near-critical paths, total and free float, schedule sensitivity, and emerging risks. Distinguish true completion drivers from secondary delays and communicate potential impacts early.
  • Recovery and Scenario Planning: Develop what-if analyses, recovery plans, acceleration options, and schedule compression scenarios. Quantify the milestone and critical-path implications of proposed decisions, changes, and mitigation actions.

  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and stakeholder-management skills

  • Startup or high-growth company experience

  • Able to build strong partnerships with technical teams and hold contributors accountable for timely, high-quality information
  • Disciplined in separating schedule facts, assumptions, risks, and management targets

  • Confident facilitating planning discussions across stakeholders with competing priorities
  • Clear and concise when communicating schedule impacts to technical teams and senior leadership
  • Detail-oriented, data-driven, and committed to schedule quality

  • Passionate about clean energy

You will work closely with process engineering, licensing, operations, safeguards, environmental compliance, construction, and business development teams to ensure radioactive waste considerations are incorporated early into facility and process design rather than addressed later in the project lifecycle.

title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer - Reactor Module
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for an experienced Mechanical Design Engineer to join our team. We are looking to fill this position immediately. Level (Engineer III/Senior) will be determined by experience.

Position Description

As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer at Oklo, you will play a central role in designing the critical hardware that enables our advanced fast reactors to operate safely and reliably. This includes technical ownership of large, multi-component weldments and assemblies that comprise the reactor module within our Aurora powerhouses—ranging from the reactor vessel to various internal support structures and primary coolant flow elements. You will be responsible for advancing these components from conceptual design through detailed design and fabrication readiness, ensuring that every element is engineered for performance, manufacturability, industrial Code compliance, and integration into Oklo’s broader reactor system. Your work will require deep engagement with cross-functional teams including structural analysts, systems engineers, materials experts, and external design and fabrication partners.

This is a high-responsibility role at the heart of our flagship product. Success in this position requires producing quality mechanical solutions in a fast-paced, startup environment where technical excellence and a collaborative mindset are equally valued.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Develop and own the design of complex mechanical components and subsystems within the reactor module
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with other engineering teams to define design and functional requirements, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and industry codes standards (e.g., ASME BPVC)
  • Use CAD tools to translate functional requirements into robust designs that meet structural, thermal, and integration constraints
  • Conduct and participate in design reviews, providing and receiving technical feedback
  • Rigorously evaluate mechanical designs to identify deficiencies and proactively propose and implement solutions
  • Generate and maintain detailed 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and bills of materials using controlled processes in PDM/PLM systems
  • Coordinate closely with analysis teams to guide and interpret thermal, structural, fatigue, and safety analyses in support of design validation
  • Perform detailed manufacturability reviews, tolerance studies, and DFM/DFA assessments to prepare components for fabrication and assembly
  • Create and maintain clear, well-written engineering documentation, including design rationales, functional requirements, reviews of historical designs, and detailed explanations of system architecture and performance
  • Work closely with fabrication partners to refine designs for cost-effective and practical production
  • Manage engagements with consultants and engineering firms to support high-fidelity analysis, ASME code compliance, and design maturity advancement
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of Oklo’s mechanical design processes, tools, and standards through feedback and development of best practices

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or higher degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline
  • 8+ years of industry experience in mechanical or structural design within sectors such as aerospace, automotive, energy, or industrial equipment
  • Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling software (e.g., Siemens NX, CATIA, SolidWorks), including part modeling, large assemblies, and detailed drawings
  • Experience with design control using PDM/PLM tools (e.g., Siemens Teamcenter, SolidWorks PDM, Windchill)

  • Perform and review pressure vessel analyses for internal and external pressure, local loads, nozzle loads, thermal gradients, buckling, fatigue, creep, and cyclic service, including design-by-analysis when appropriate.

  • Perform and review steady-state and transient thermal analyses addressing heat loss, insulation, heat tracing, temperature gradients, heat-up, cooldown, and abnormal thermal conditions.

  • Select and qualify materials for high-temperature and corrosive service, considering molten-salt compatibility, oxidation, thermal aging, creep, fatigue, radiation exposure where applicable, weldability, and fabrication constraints.

  • Design and review vessels, piping, nozzles, flanges, closures, transitions, supports, anchors, restraints, expansion joints, bellows, penetrations, and other pressure-boundary components.

  • Support commissioning, troubleshooting, and root-cause evaluations involving high-temperature piping, pressure vessels, and pressure boundaries.

  • Mentor other engineers and provide technical leadership in high-temperature piping and vessel design, analysis, materials, fabrication, and engineering judgment.
