  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

  • 10+ years of mechanical engineering experience with process piping, pressure vessels, or high-temperature systems, including responsibility for piping stress, pressure vessel, thermal, or mechanical stress analyses.

  • Working knowledge of applicable ASME codes and standards, including ASME B31.3 and ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII.

  • Experience developing and reviewing calculations, specifications, data sheets, drawings, and fabrication-ready design packages.

  • Experience with materials selection, welding, fabrication, nondestructive examination, pressure testing, and inspection of piping or vessels.

  • Ability to independently evaluate analytical results, code compliance, design assumptions, failure modes, and technical margins.

  • Experience coordinating piping and vessel interfaces with process, structural, equipment, instrumentation and controls, operations, and supplier teams.

  • Strong technical writing, communication, and engineering judgment.

Position Description

The Senior Neutronics Engineer is responsible for developing and executing neutronics analyses supporting the design, optimization, operation, and safety evaluation of an isotope production reactor. The engineer will perform analyses to support core design, fuel cycle, target performance, shielding, and sensitivity/uncertainty quantification across the reactor lifecycle and isotope production facility.

This role requires close collaboration with thermal hydraulics, mechanical design, materials, isotope processing, operations, safety, and licensing teams. The engineer will translate system and production objectives into analysis requirements; develop appropriate computational models and methods; and produce technically sound, traceable, and defensible results. Areas of analysis include criticality, depletion, isotope production, target optimization, shielding, activation, source term, and sensitivity/uncertainty analysis.

The isotope division is a small but growing team so the candidate must be capable of operating in a highly iterative and independent environment.

description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Sodium Test Engineer to join our team in Idaho Falls.

Position Description

Oklo is transforming the future of energy, and we are looking for a Sodium Test Engineer to develop and operate test platforms that support advanced nuclear technology development.

In this role, you will lead or support the design, fabrication, commissioning, operation, and modification of experimental systems involving molten sodium with travel up to 10%.

The ideal candidate has direct knowledge or hands-on experience with molten sodium, or other molten alkali-metal systems. This experience may include system design, laboratory research, test operations, equipment development, chemistry control, component testing, maintenance, or decommissioning. The successful candidate will understand the unique operating, materials, cleanliness, containment, and safety considerations associated with reactive liquid metals.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Test Program Development: Translate engineering data requirements into executable tests. Prepare test plans, laboratory procedures, work instructions, equipment requirements, inspection points, and data-collection methods for materials-characterization activities.
  • Test Execution: Lead or support test setup, readiness reviews, equipment checkout, specimen installation, startup, monitoring, shutdown, and post-test activities.
  • Data Validation and Analysis: Review raw data for completeness and validity, identify anomalies, assess measurement uncertainty, calculate material properties, evaluate repeatability, and compare results with expected behavior or established requirements.
  • Technical Reporting: Prepare test reports, materials evaluations, failure-analysis reports, engineering memos, data summaries, and recommendations. Clearly document methods, assumptions, deviations, results, uncertainties, and conclusions.
  • Laboratory Development: Help establish and improve materials-laboratory capabilities, equipment-maintenance programs, calibration practices, specimen-storage methods, test templates, and safe operating procedures.

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, nuclear engineering, materials engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Ability to read and interpret piping and instrumentation diagrams, process-flow diagrams, equipment drawings, electrical schematics, instrument diagrams, and vendor documentation.
  • Ability to lift, move, and position objects weighing up to 30 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Direct hands-on experience operating molten-sodium test loops or experimental sodium systems.
  • Experience with high-temperature piping, heat tracing, insulation, freeze protection, thermal expansion, and temperature-control systems.

description:

Position Description

The Technical Program Manager will lead the development and execution of technical projects with U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories and other government partners, turning strategic opportunities into well-defined agreements, work packages, and delivered results.

The Technical Program Manager will serve as the primary point of contact and, where appropriate, principal investigator for national laboratory collaborations. You will work across Recycling engineering teams and interface closely with Legal, Procurement, Finance, and Recycling leadership to negotiate, establish, and execute contracts, cooperative agreements, and related project mechanisms.

This role is for a technically fluent program leader who can develop new opportunities, shape ambiguous ideas into executable projects, and manage complex external partnerships from concept through closeout. Success requires strong technical judgment grounded in relevant experience, disciplined delivery management, and the ability to navigate technical, contractual, financial, and legal considerations in a fast-moving, highly regulated environment.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Serve as Oklo's primary point of contact and, as assigned, principal investigator for national laboratory projects and other government-funded collaborations related to spent nuclear fuel recycling and pyroprocessing technology.

title: Test Process Equipment Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Test Process Equipment Engineer to join our team in Idaho Falls.

Position Description

Oklo is transforming the future of energy, and we are looking for a Test Process Equipment Engineer to support the design, fabrication, commissioning, operation, and modification of test platforms used in advanced nuclear technology development.

In this role, you will be responsible for process and mechanical equipment throughout the full test-platform lifecycle—from defining requirements and developing conceptual designs through equipment procurement, fabrication, installation, commissioning, test execution, and system improvement with 10% travel.

The ideal candidate combines strong engineering fundamentals with practical, hands-on experience. Position Description

The Thermal-Hydraulics and Safety Analysis Engineer is responsible for developing and executing systems-level thermal-hydraulic analyses that support the safety case, design basis, and licensing of Oklo's reactor systems. This engineer will evaluate reactor and plant response during normal operation, anticipated operational occurrences, and postulated accident conditions using codes such as RELAP5 and other systems-analysis tools.

This role combines hands-on transient modeling with safety-methodology development. The engineer will establish modeling approaches, assess code and model applicability, quantify uncertainty, and produce clear, auditable technical documentation suitable for licensing applications and regulatory review. The engineer will work closely with safety, licensing, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, controls, and system-design teams to connect analysis assumptions and acceptance criteria to an evolving reactor design.

This position is focused on thermal-hydraulic safety analysis and licensing support. It does not own source-term, radiological-consequence, or severe-accident progression analysis, although collaboration with engineers performing those analyses may be required.

The isotope engineering team is a small but growing team, so the candidate must be capable of operating in a highly iterative and independent environment.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Develop, maintain, and execute systems-level thermal-hydraulic models of reactor and plant behavior using RELAP5 or comparable analysis codes.

  • Analyze normal operating conditions, anticipated operational occurrences, design-basis events, and selected beyond-design-basis conditions relevant to the thermal-hydraulic safety case.

  • Develop event-specific analysis plans, including initial and boundary conditions, assumptions, acceptance criteria, figures of merit, and treatment of uncertainties.

  • Develop and document thermal-hydraulic safety-analysis methods, modeling guidance, and engineering practices appropriate to advanced reactor licensing.

  • Establish and justify code, model, and correlation applicability for the physical phenomena and operating regimes being evaluated.

  • Perform model verification, validation, sensitivity studies, uncertainty analyses, scaling evaluations, and comparisons with experiments, benchmarks, hand calculations, or higher-fidelity analyses. Identify gaps in available methods, data, and validation evidence, and define practical plans to close those gaps.

  • Translate regulatory requirements and safety acceptance criteria into defensible analysis requirements and technical evaluation strategies.

  • Prepare high-quality calculation packages, methodology documents, safety-analysis reports, licensing-application content, and responses to regulator questions.

  • Evaluate design changes and provide timely feedback on their effects on transient response, safety margins, system performance, and the licensing basis.

  • Collaborate with reactor physics, fuel, controls, mechanical, thermal-hydraulics, safety, and licensing engineers on coupled analyses and interface conditions.

  • Develop scripts and automated workflows for model generation, execution, post-processing, regression testing, and configuration control.

  • Review safety analyses and models prepared by internal contributors, vendors, and external partners.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in nuclear, mechanical, chemical, or aerospace engineering, or a closely related technical field.

  • Five or more years of relevant experience in reactor thermal-hydraulics, nuclear safety analysis, reactor transient analysis, or a closely related field. A relevant advanced degree may substitute for a portion of the professional experience.

  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing systems-level transient models using RELAP5.

  • Strong foundation in heat transfer, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and reactor thermal-hydraulics.

  • Experience defining and analyzing reactor transients or accident scenarios, including initial conditions, boundary conditions, equipment response, operator or control actions, and acceptance criteria.

  • Experience evaluating the reasonableness and applicability of models, correlations, assumptions, and results rather than treating analysis software as a black box.

  • Experience documenting engineering analyses in clear, reviewable technical reports or calculation packages.

  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across engineering and licensing disciplines.

  • Experience with verification and validation, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, scaling, bias evaluation, or code applicability assessments.

  • Familiarity with experiment design, separate-effects and integral-effects testing, benchmark problems, and the use of test data to validate analytical methods.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting NRC or DOE licensing applications, audits, topical or methodology reports, requests for additional information, or other regulatory interactions.

  • Fluency with Python or another language used for model automation, data analysis, visualization, and quality checks.

  • Competency with modern software engineering practices, including version control, automated testing, reproducible computing environments, and continuous integration.

  • Experience working under a nuclear quality-assurance program or with safety-related analysis software and records.

  • Experience mentoring other analysts or providing technical review of safety-analysis work.

Competencies

We are looking for a Thermal-Hydraulics and Safety Analysis Engineer who is:

  • Skilled at developing and interpreting systems-level reactor transient analyses.

  • Able to connect thermal-hydraulic behavior, safety functions, acceptance criteria, and licensing conclusions.

  • Methodical about verification, validation, uncertainty, configuration control, and technical documentation.

  • Comfortable making conservative but technically defensible assumptions when information is incomplete.

  • Able to distinguish important safety drivers from modeling detail that does not materially affect a conclusion.

  • Comfortable explaining model limitations and uncertainty to designers, reviewers, and regulators.

  • Collaborative and effective at working across safety, licensing, design, reactor physics, and analysis teams.

  • Passionate about clean energy, and about making domestic supply of national-need and therapeutic isotope production a reality.

  • Willing and able to learn quickly, think differently, and do things in new ways.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

  • An excellent writer who can write in a modern active voice, and able to communicate technical content and results verbally.
